result:
No. Redis solves state sharing across processes or hosts, and you have neither. A single writer with SQLite as the durable store already gives you serialized writes and crash recovery.

What you'd get instead: a second source of truth that can disagree with SQLite, a network hop on every read, serialization cost at the boundary, and a new failure domain that takes the service down when it's unavailable. None of that buys correctness you don't already have.

If the motive is read speed, use ETS. It is in-process, no serialization, and rebuilt from SQLite on boot exactly like your current state. If it's pub/sub, use Registry or `:pg`. If it's caching expensive computations, ETS with a TTL sweeper.

Revisit if any of these become true: you run more than one node and they need shared state, working set outgrows RAM, or an external system needs to read your state without going through your API. At that point compare Redis against Mnesia and a read replica of SQLite before committing.
